newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-ELLEM WINS WOMEN'S 200 BREASTSTROKE WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-ELLEM WINS WOMEN'S 200 BREASTSTROKE WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Fifteen-year-old Kristy Ellem kept Australia in command at the world short-course swimming championships on Friday, winning the women's 200 metres breaststroke by a vast margin.
Ellem inherited the title from her training partner Samantha Riley to give Australia their fourth title of the four-day meeting.
Ellem took charge from the start, with Larisa Lacusta of Romania in vain pursuit as her closest challenger throughout the eight-length race in the 25-metre Scandinavium arena pool.
The Australian stretched away to win by nearly three seconds in two minutes 22.68 seconds.

Lacusta took the silver in 2:25.60 -- just 0.02 seconds ahead of Poland's Alicja Peczak, the European short-course champion, who repeated her bronze medal performance of the 1995 world short-course championships in Rio de Janeiro.
American Amanda Beard, double breaststroke silver medallist at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics, was never seriously in contention and finished fifth.
